reasons: Fixed health figures are shown as if they were real.
The greeting does not depend on the time of day.

terms.meaning: A shared place in the app where state such as the signed-in user is kept.
Loading part of a page only when it is needed, to make the first load faster.
A grey placeholder shape shown while content loads.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and lazy-loaded widgets
sections.what: Brings in icons, cards and the user store, then sets up four widgets to load only when needed, each with a placeholder while loading.
sections.why: The comment says the widgets are split out for code splitting, which makes the first load smaller.
sections.watch_out: The quick actions widget is not drawn on the server, so a placeholder may show briefly.

sections.name: DashboardHome (part 1)
sections.title: Greeting and fixed health numbers
sections.what: Shows a greeting using the first word of the user's name, a fixed status sentence, and two metric cards with fixed values: a health score of 84 and 7.5 hours of sleep.
sections.why: Likely reason: placeholder content while real data is wired up. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The numbers are typed in, not read from records, so they will not match the patient's actual health data.

sections.name: DashboardHome (part 2)
sections.title: Adherence card and recent reports
sections.what: Shows a 'Weekly Adherence' card with a fixed value of 95 percent and a +5% badge, followed by a 'Recent Reports' list. The list has two hard-coded entries, both labelled Full Blood Count from Max Healthcare, one marked Normal and one marked 2 Flags.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The fixed values look like placeholder content for a design mock-up rather than real patient data.
sections.watch_out: These numbers do not come from the server. A user could see a made-up adherence score or report and believe it is their real data.

sections.name: DashboardHome (part 3)
sections.title: Upcoming appointments placeholder
sections.what: Shows an empty-state box saying no appointments are scheduled this week, with a Book Visit button. The button does nothing in this code.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It appears to be a visual placeholder for a future feature.
sections.watch_out: The message is fixed text, so it will say no appointments even when some exist.

sections.name: MetricCard
sections.title: Reusable metric card
sections.what: A small card layout that shows a title, a big value, a unit, a trend badge and an icon. It is defined in this file but the page does not use it in the displayed sections.
sections.why: Likely reason: a reusable layout for summary numbers. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Its props are typed as any, so a wrong value will not be caught while writing code.

sections.name: FileText
sections.title: Local icon wrapper for FileText
sections.what: Wraps the FileText icon from the icon library so it accepts size and class settings. It is used in the Recent Reports list.
sections.why: The code comment says the icon was not imported, so this wrapper was added as a workaround. The real reason for the duplicate import is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The file imports FileText as another name at the bottom and also defines its own FileText. Removing either one can break the page, and the duplication is confusing for anyone reading it.

summary: The home screen after sign-in: a greeting, quick actions, and health cards. Several health numbers are fixed values, not real data.
purpose: Gives a quick overview when a patient opens the app.
why: Likely reason: the fixed numbers stand in until real data is connected. This is not stated in the code.
how: Reads the user's name from the store and shows the first word in the greeting. Shows quick actions and some widgets loaded on demand. Shows two metric cards with fixed values.
inputs: The user's name from the store.
risks: The health score of 84, sleep of 7.5 hours, trend values, the 'stable' sentence and the 'Syncing with Apple Health' text are typed in, so they may not match the patient's real data. The greeting always says Good morning.
debug: Numbers that do not change with data are expected. To fix, replace the typed values with values from the server.
